title: Katie Boulter Wins Rain-Delayed Match at the Japan Open
summary:
British tennis player Katie Boulter earned a strong first-round win at the Japan Open in Osaka, but she had to wait an extra day to finish it.

Boulter was playing Himeno Sakatsume, a Japanese player who was the home crowd's favorite. On Monday, Boulter had already won the first set and was leading 3-1 in the second set when bad weather stopped play. Rain made it impossible to continue that night.

The two players returned to the court on Tuesday. Boulter finished the job and won the match 6-3, 6-1.

"Yesterday was a tough spot to end at," Boulter said afterward. She explained that she had wanted to keep playing on Monday night, but the rain did not allow it. "It meant that I had to have the same mindset again today and just try to get over the line and focus on getting through the match," she said. "I think I did that."

She also said she was glad the match did not go to a third set.

The numbers show how well Boulter handled pressure. A break point is a chance for the player receiving the serve to win a game. Boulter won five of her nine break points. Sakatsume, who entered the tournament as a wild card, which means she was given a special invitation to play, had 13 break points but won only one.

Boulter, who is 30, will face Viktorija Golubic of Switzerland in the second round.

In other tennis news, world number nine Iga Swiatek pulled out of the Ningbo Open because of a thigh injury. That makes it harder for her to reach the WTA Finals, which feature the top eight players of the year and will take place in Indian Wells from November 8 to 15.
why_it_matters: Boulter's win shows how athletes must stay focused through interruptions, and late-season results and injuries help decide who reaches the year's biggest final event.
